main_text.head: EPITAPHIA.
Io. Caluini Epicedium, à G. Buchanano scriptum.

p.i: SI quis erit nullos superesse à funere manes Qui putet, aut si forte putet sic viuit vt Orcum Speret, & æternas Stygio sub gurgite pœnas, Is merito sua fata fleat, sua funera ploret Viuus, & ad charos luctum transmittat amicos. At nos, inuitis quanquam sis raptus amicis Ante diem, magnis quanuis inuiderit aufis Mors, te flere nefas, Caluine, & funera vana Ludibrio pompa, & miseris onerare querelis. Liber enim curis, terrena & pondere molis, Astra tenes, propiusque Deo, quem mente colebas Nunc frueris, puroque vides in lumine purum Lumen, & infusi satiatus Numinis haustu Exigis æternam sine follicitudine vitam: Quam neque deiciunt luctus, nec tollit inani Ebria lætitia spes, exanimántve timores: Queque animo offundit morbi contagia corpus. Hanc ego qua curis te lux exemit acerbis Natalem iure appellem, qua raptus in astra In patriam remeas, & post fastidia duri Exilij, mortis iam mens secura secunda

page.notes: Small marks in the left margin beside lines (Liber, Astra, Ante) look like printer's marks or ornaments, not notes; left out. Verse stanza kept as one paragraph with lines separated by line breaks. The word "secura" has a Cyrillic-looking a in the scan's typography; it was copied as a Latin a. Right margin shows show-through from the facing page and was left out. Lower-right "Fortu-" taken as the catchword. The page has no running head.
